doc.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Jazz as a melting pot, not a pure canon
summary: Citing Jack Walrath, he rejects racial purification and tells Russian players to bring their own rhythms.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well you said it about five times already, that the music was the focus. That the music brought them together I would guess.

And I mean the thing that ultimately anything that divides, I mean that’s another irony is that the whole thing about jazz is that it was kind of melting pot. What keeps it alive is all the influences coming in. When you get into this like racial purification it’s kind of like Nazi talk. I mean that’s the opposite of art, the opposite of something living, breathing. It’s got to take in, to quote Jack Walrath, who was kind of like saying, he was like speaking against this idea of trying to form, saying that this is jazz, this isn’t jazz, and that there should be this canon and a definition of what it is and what it isn’t. He’s saying look, the St. Louis Blues, from 1905, and the second strain is a tango. That says it right there. What is this purity stuff? There’s nothing pure about it. It’s anybody who feels that it belongs to them, and whatever they can bring — you know, European — I mean it’s ridiculous because there’s great European players now. And I heard these guys from © Fillius Jazz Archive -23-

Russia, they sent me a record, really good players. And I wrote back to them and I said this record is great but it sounds like it was made in New York. I said you know like there’s so many interesting rhythmic things in the music from your part of the world, put some of that in there.
Don’t be ashamed, don’t feel that you have to do—

I mean yeah, don’t copy, bring what you’ve got into it and it’ll just make it stronger for everybody. And of course that happens. That will happen. But whether that gets focused on, I mean at this moment, it’s like other things get more attention but that’s just the way it is right now.
